Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image is EDIT TARGET: existing Living Room02 looking from black steel doors towards kitchen, sofa large on LEFT, coffer/TV/hat/shelf on right.
Create ONE controlled SOFA UPHOLSTERY COLOUR comparison, one photorealistic landscape photograph. Change ONLY THE SOFA'S MAIN UPHOLSTERY COLOUR on all seat/back cushions, arms and body; keep its EXACT straight three-seat shape, proportions, seams, timber feet, woven fabric texture, position and camera unchanged. This is a fabric colour trial, NOT permission to introduce a new sofa design.
Preserve ALL other pixels as closely as possible: user's round clock, exact beige/grey wall paint, original white mouldings/cornice/ceiling/downlights, black steel glazed doorframe, oak floor, colourful brick/ochre/slate geometric kilim rug and exact footprint, old oak coffer below mounted TV, existing black/timber ladder shelf with user's ORIGINAL ornaments (dark seated figure, copper pots, scene plate, red glass piece, silver-toned figurine, animal miniatures and books), red Vietnamese hat ABOVE shelf, monstera, vintage turned-leg coffee table with one bowl, small marble side table and brass/linen lamp, kitchen/dining/garden furniture and fixtures.
Keep current three DECORATIVE cushions EXACTLY as in input (muted rust, olive and flax striped) and oatmeal throw unchanged; recolour sofa seat/back upholstery only, not accent cushions. Do not swap/remove cushion/throw or add objects. Keep same shadows, photography exposure, daylight and warm lamp, identical room lighting. Never repaint wall or darken entire image to simulate colour. No repaint, room alterations, extra sofa, collage, labels, text or watermark. Natural real matte woven fabric, detailed texture, no shiny synthetic look.
OPTION A: SOFA ONLY becomes a sophisticated muted PETROL BLUE, a medium-deep blue with a subtle green undertone. Clearly a blue sofa (not olive, grey, black, navy, bright teal or turquoise). Low saturation but rich enough to make this room different from beige. Colour should pick up the subdued slate/indigo in the rug while contrasting warmly with oak and brick red. Retain same fabric weave, no velvet/shiny material change.
